---
title: "Engineer course setup"
subtitle: "One locked environment and one clean kernel per Chapter"
---

## Install the beta wheel

Use CPython 3.12 and download the matching wheel from
[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/scnsim/releases). The provided
platforms are Linux x86_64 (manylinux 2.28) and macOS arm64 (deployment target
macOS 12). These platform tags identify the binary target; they do not imply
that every operating-system version or circuit workload has been exercised.

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python /path/to/scnsim-wheel.whl
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python jupyterlab ipykernel
.venv/bin/python -m jupyterlab
```

Use a fresh environment rather than installing over a running notebook kernel.
Select that environment's Python kernel. A matching SCNSim wheel needs no C++
compiler. Compatible dependencies install normally; a pure-Python dependency
build is different from compiling a native extension. If a native dependency
must be built from source on an unsupported platform, that installation is not
covered by the compiler-free wheel path.

The manual diagram display uses the notebook's IPython rich-display support.
It does not require a separate GUI figure manager.

## Work from the course source

For the matching beta course, select the `v1.0.0b1` source when it is published.
The `develop` branch follows ongoing development and can differ from a release.
A source installation builds SCNSim's native extension and requires a C++17
compiler; it is separate from installing a prebuilt wheel.

From the selected source checkout, install the existing locked course tools
and start Jupyter from the repository root:

```bash
uv sync --locked --group course-generation
uv run --locked --with jupyterlab jupyter lab
```

The `jupyterlab` package is ephemeral tooling for that command; it is not added
to SCNSim or its lock. An editor-provided Jupyter frontend may instead open the
Chapter Notebook after the locked sync. Select the repository's `.venv` Python
kernel, restart it, and use **Run All**. The course source also contains the
manual layout helpers used by its diagram cells; these are ordinary Example
code, not an automatically installed layout service.

Read the [Simulation conventions](../../docs/concepts/simulation-conventions.qmd)
before interpreting S/Y/Z, phase, PTC, or loaded roots. The explicit selected
View governs all three matrix surfaces.

Chapters 1–4 form the mainline course; Chapters 5–8 are optional
continuations. Chapters 1–7 are separate clean-kernel execution units.
Chapter 8 instead has
an explicit two-kernel procedure: execute Lesson 1, stop that kernel, then use
a second fresh kernel to run only Lesson 2 against the same preserved working
directory. The shorter web Lessons are reading views over ordered source
fragments and are not independently runnable.

JAX CPU is the default numerical backend. A cold request can include runtime
preparation and compilation. An explicitly selected Julia operation may also
prepare its separately configured Julia runtime. A relative path such as
`workspaces/engineer-chapter-02` is resolved from the process's current working
directory. That workspace is Result evidence, not a disposable calculation
cache: ignoring it in Git neither deletes nor backs it up, and exact later
resolution requires its preserved bytes.

For ordinary design iteration, classify the change before reusing a workspace.
A new `ParameterSet` reuses the same captured Plan, Run, and Views. Changing an
objective expression, comparison, target, scale, or weight constructs a new
`OptimizationSpec` on those same objects. Changing model defaults, topology,
Ports, or a captured parameter definition requires rebuilding the inputs,
Plan, Run, Views, and Specs. A newly rebuilt Plan's old View or ParameterRef is
foreign even when a Python name or printed declaration looks the same.
That rebuild may happen in the same kernel, but it must use the newly returned
ParameterRef, Plan, Run, View, and Spec handles together; never mix a handle
retained from the earlier Plan into the rebuilt object graph.

With `versioned=False`, constructing that different Plan at the same workspace
path deliberately replaces the prior active Plan evidence; it does not erase
all evidence on every request. Requests on one Plan remain distinct by their
canonical request identity. Use `versioned=True` when multiple Plan versions
must coexist, and preserve the workspace bytes required by each version.
Reusing the same variable names and workspace path in one live kernel is legal
when the Plan identity is unchanged; a kernel restart is not an identity
operation and does not repair a foreign handle.
